text: I will advise you seriously, as a friend of some experience, and I will converse with you cheerfully as a companion; the authority of a parent shall forever be laid aside; for, wherever it is exerted, it is useless; since, if you have neither sense nor sentiments enough to follow my advice as a friend, your unwilling obedience to my orders as a father will be a very awkward and unavailing one both to yourself and me.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter LXXXVII, to his son, London, October 24, Old Style 1749
